transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT service_name, 'abn' AS p, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) http5xx FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY service_name UNION ALL SELECT service_name, 'norm', count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY service_name ORDER BY service_name, p

content.text: Frontend and search are much slower in the incident window, and span volume is down overall. Next I'll look at per-endpoint latency and the caller-callee span pairs.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, max(duration)/1e6 max_ms, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), max(duration)/1e6, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The key signal: `search` calls `rate.Rate/GetRates` and waits about 1.7 s, but the `rate` server span is only about 0.5 ms. The delay sits between the two services. Next I'll check the network and pod metrics for that connection.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv, round(max(value),2) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY metric
SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY metric, service_name

content.text: Logs contain no errors. I'll read the messages from `search` and `rate` directly, since they're the services on the slow path.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, message, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: The `rate` log messages look normal. To locate where the 1.7 s gap sits, I'll line up one slow trace's spans by start time and duration.

input.query: WITH slow AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='search' AND span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT t.time, t.service_name, t.span_name, t.attr_span_kind, t.duration/1e6 ms, t.span_id, t.parent_span_id, t.attr_k8s_pod_name FROM abnormal_traces t JOIN slow USING(trace_id) ORDER BY t.time

content.text: The `rate` server span is missing from this trace, so the slow calls may never reach the server-side handler. I'll check how often a `search` → `rate` client span has a matching server span, and compare durations for matched and unmatched calls.

input.query: SELECT c.span_name, (s.span_id IS NOT NULL) has_server, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,2) avg_client_ms, round(min(c.duration)/1e6,2) min_ms, round(max(c.duration)/1e6,2) max_ms FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.service_name='search' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: Every `search` → `rate` call that has a linked server span is slow (≥1.35 s), while the server handler itself takes about 0.5 ms. I'll compare start times of matched pairs to see whether the delay falls before the server starts.

input.query: SELECT round(avg(epoch_ms(s.time)-epoch_ms(c.time)),1) avg_start_gap_ms, round(min(epoch_ms(s.time)-epoch_ms(c.time)),1) min_gap, round(max(epoch_ms(s.time)-epoch_ms(c.time)),1) max_gap, round(avg(c.duration/1e6 - s.duration/1e6),1) avg_client_minus_server_ms, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates'

SELECT round(avg(epoch_ms(s.time)-epoch_ms(c.time)),1) avg_start_gap_ms, round(avg(c.duration/1e6 - s.duration/1e6),2) avg_client_minus_server_ms, count(*) n FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates'

content.text: The entire delay occurs before the `rate` server receives the request (about 1737 ms gap versus 0.1 ms normally), and the server's own work is unchanged. To separate a wire-level delay from an application-layer hold, I'll check which network-level metrics exist for `search` and `rate`.

input.query: SELECT DISTINCT metric, 'sum' t FROM abnormal_metrics_sum UNION SELECT DISTINCT metric, 'gauge' FROM abnormal_metrics UNION SELECT DISTINCT metric, 'hist' FROM abnormal_metrics_histogram ORDER BY 1

content.text: There is a `k8s.pod.network.io` metric. I'll compare it, plus CPU and memory, for `search`, `rate`, `frontend`, and `reservation` across both periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),1) avgv, round(max(value),1) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.io') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), round(avg(value),1), round(max(value),1) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.io') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),4) avgv, round(max(value),4) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.memory.rss') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, count(*), round(avg(value),4), round(max(value),4) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.memory.rss') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Network I/O and CPU/memory are flat across both periods, so there is no resource saturation. I'll run one more check to confirm the user-facing impact on `/hotels` and that its latency comes from the `search` call.

input.query: SELECT p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,1) avg_ms FROM (SELECT 'abn' p,* FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm',* FROM normal_traces) WHERE (service_name='frontend' AND span_name IN ('HTTP /hotels','search.Search/Nearby')) OR (service_name='search' AND span_name='search.Search/Nearby' AND attr_span_kind='Server') OR (service_name='reservation' AND span_name LIKE 'reservation.Reservation/%' AND attr_span_kind='Server') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1
